title: Rooted
subtitle: Five readings on growing in Christ
author: Sample book

chapters.title: Hungry for the Word
paras: > As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby. [[1 Peter 2:2]]

Every living thing grows by what it takes in. A seed needs water, a child needs bread, and a believer needs the Word of God. Peter does not tell us to admire the Word or to keep it on a shelf. He tells us to desire it the way a newborn desires milk: often, simply, and without embarrassment.

Hunger is a sign of life. When our appetite for Scripture fades, it is rarely because the Word has changed. More often other things have filled us first: noise, worry, entertainment, even good work done in our own strength. Jesus answered the tempter with the words of Moses, that man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God [[Matthew 4:4]].
## Begin small, begin daily

Spiritual nourishment is less about long sessions and more about steady ones. A single chapter read slowly, with a question in your heart, will feed you more than ten chapters skimmed. Read until a verse stops you. Stay there. Ask what it shows you about God, and what it asks of you today.

The psalmist hid the Word in his heart so that he would not sin against God [[Psalm 119:11]]. What we store, the Holy Spirit can bring back to us when we need it: in a hospital corridor, a hard conversation, or a sleepless night.
## For reflection
When during the day are you most hungry and most quiet? Give that time to the Word this week, even if it is only ten minutes.

chapters.title: Prayer as Daily Bread
paras: > Give us this day our daily bread. [[Matthew 6:11]]

Jesus taught His disciples to ask for bread one day at a time. Israel gathered manna each morning, and it would not keep until the next [[Exodus 16:19-21]]. Grace works the same way. Yesterday’s prayer was real, but today needs its own.

Prayer is not only asking. It is the place where we bring our whole life before the Father and receive His life in return. In prayer we confess, we give thanks, we listen, and we learn to want what He wants.
## Pray the way you breathe

Paul urges believers to pray without ceasing [[1 Thessalonians 5:17]]. This does not mean we never stop speaking. It means our heart stays turned toward God through the day: a short word of thanks at the start of a task, a cry for help in the middle of it, a blessing over the people we meet.
Set times of prayer give shape to this. Many find it helpful to begin the day with Scripture and prayer together, letting the passage they read become the words they pray.
## For reflection
Choose one verse from your reading today and turn it into a short prayer. Pray it again at midday and before you sleep.

chapters.title: Abiding in the Vine
paras: > I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing. [[John 15:5]]

A branch does not strain to produce grapes. It stays joined to the vine, and the life of the vine flows through it. Jesus uses this picture to show that spiritual growth is first a matter of connection, not effort.

To abide is to remain, to make your home somewhere. We abide in Christ when His words abide in us [[John 15:7]], when we keep His commandments and remain in His love [[John 15:10]]. It is a daily choice to stay close.
## The work of the Gardener

Jesus also says the Father prunes every branch that bears fruit, so that it may bear more. Pruning can feel like loss. A habit is cut away, a plan is closed, a comfort is removed. Yet the Gardener’s hand is never careless. He cuts so that the life of the vine can reach further.
## For reflection
Where do you sense the Father pruning you in this season? Thank Him for His care, and ask for grace to remain close while He works.

chapters.title: Growing Through Seasons
paras: > To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven. [[Ecclesiastes 3:1]]

Trees do not grow at the same pace all year. There are seasons of blossom and seasons of bare branches, and both are part of growth. The believer’s life has seasons too: times of joy and harvest, and times of waiting, testing, and quiet.

James writes that the trying of our faith produces patience, and that patience should be allowed to finish its work [[James 1:2-4]]. Hard seasons are not wasted. Roots go deepest when the surface is dry.
## Stay planted

The blessed person of Psalm 1 is like a tree planted by rivers of water, that brings forth fruit in its season, whose leaf does not wither [[Psalm 1:3]]. Notice the words: in its season. Fruit comes in God’s timing, but the tree stays planted all year long.
In winter seasons, keep the simple disciplines: the Word, prayer, fellowship, and worship. They may feel small, but they keep you rooted until spring.
## For reflection
Name the season you are in. What would it look like to stay planted in it, rather than trying to hurry out of it?

chapters.title: Bearing Fruit That Remains
paras: > Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain. [[John 15:16]]
Growth is never only for ourselves. A fruit tree feeds others. The life Christ grows in us is meant to bless our families, our church, and the people around us who do not yet know Him.

Paul names the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance [[Galatians 5:22-23]]. These grow quietly, often unnoticed by the one bearing them, but they are seen by everyone nearby.
## Fruit that lasts
Jesus wants fruit that remains. That kind of fruit comes from lives that keep returning to Him: rooted in the Word, sustained by prayer, abiding in the Vine, and patient through every season.
As you close this short book, ask the Lord to make you someone who feeds others, the way He has fed you.
## For reflection
Who is one person you can encourage this week with something God has shown you? Reach out to them before the week ends.
